Sardis-Turkey.name: Sardis
Sardis-Turkey.evidence_basis: LBA Hermus Valley town expanding under the Mermnad Lydian kings into a massive ~110-140 ha fortified metropolis with gold refineries and royal citadel before Cyrus's 546 BC conquest (Cahill & Greenewalt 2016).

Hattusa-Turkey.name: Hattusa
Hattusa-Turkey.evidence_basis: MBA karum town of ~25 ha (Palmisano 2017) expanding to ~180-185 ha walled imperial capital in the 14th-13th c. BC (Schachner 2017; Mielke 2011; Glatz 2009), collapsing c. 1180 BC to a small Iron Age fortified settlement on Buyukkale and Buyukkaya (Genz 2004).

Tyre-Lebanon.name: Tyre
Tyre-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Multi-storey densely built Phoenician island fortress plus mainland Ushu (Palaetyrus) peaking as Mediterranean trade metropolis before Nebuchadnezzar II's 586-573 BC siege (Bikai 1978; Markoe 2000).

Miletus-Turkey.name: Miletus
Miletus-Turkey.evidence_basis: LBA Minoan-Mycenaean port of Millawanda (~15 ha) growing into Archaic Ionia's premier maritime metropolis covering ~90-110 ha across the peninsula and Kalabaktepe (Gorman 2001; Greaves 2002).

Marib-Yemen.name: Marib
Marib-Yemen.evidence_basis: Largest South Arabian capital spanning ~98-110 ha within a 4.5 km wall circuit sustained by the Great Dam oasis (~9,600 ha irrigated land; Vogt; Breton; Schiettecatte 2011).

Damascus-Syria.name: Damascus
Damascus-Syria.evidence_basis: Major Ghouta oasis city attested in LBA Amarna archives, surging as hegemonic Aramean capital under Bar-Hadad and Hazael before Tiglath-Pileser III's 732 BC conquest and Assyrian-Babylonian provincial recovery (Pitard 1987; Younger 2016).

Sidon-Lebanon.name: Sidon
Sidon-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Major coastal Phoenician city-state (~20-25 ha dense urban tell and harbours; Doumet-Serhal), sacked by Esarhaddon in 677 BC and rebounding rapidly in the 6th c. BC (Markoe 2000).

Kanesh-Turkey.name: Kanesh
Kanesh-Turkey.evidence_basis: EB III mound of ~21 ha (Makowski 2014) expanding in MBA Old Assyrian Colony period to ~170 ha total mound plus densely settled karum lower town (Ozguc 2005; Barjamovic 2011), contracting after c. 1725 BC destructions and reviving as an Iron Age Tabal centre.

Gordium-Turkey.name: Gordium
Gordium-Turkey.evidence_basis: Bronze Age mound expanding in the Early/Middle Phrygian royal period to a 13.5 ha fortified citadel plus lower and outer towns exceeding 100 ha total footprint (Rose 2017; Kealhofer 2005).

Qatna-Syria.name: Qatna
Qatna-Syria.evidence_basis: Massive 110 ha square-ramparted royal capital of central Syria with monumental MBA/LBA palace and archives, sacked by Suppiluliuma I c. 1340 BC and partially revived in Iron II (Morandi Bonacossi 2007; Pfalzner).

Salamis-Cyprus.name: Salamis
Salamis-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Founded c. 1075 BC succeeding Enkomi as eastern Cyprus's premier harbour city-kingdom, expanding rapidly in the Cypro-Geometric and Archaic royal tomb era (Karageorghis; Iacovou).

Turkmen-Karahoyuk-Turkey.name: Turkmen-Karahoyuk
Turkmen-Karahoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Intensive TISP/KRASP survey documents a 30 ha MBA mound quadrupling to ~125-150 ha in LBA (candidate for Tarhuntassa) and MIA under Great King Hartapu, before contracting to ~50 ha in the LIA (Osborne et al. 2020; Massa et al. 2020).

Aleppo-Syria.name: Aleppo
Aleppo-Syria.evidence_basis: Capital of the Amorite Kingdom of Yamhad (Mari texts), Hittite viceregal seat, and major Storm-God sanctuary centre beneath the Aleppo Citadel (Kohlmeyer; Hawkins 2011).

Jerusalem-Israel.name: Jerusalem
Jerusalem-Israel.evidence_basis: MBA/LBA ~5 ha highland town (Urusalim) expanding after 722 BC northern refugee influx across the Western Hill to ~60-65 ha (~18,000-22,000) before Nebuchadnezzar's 586 BC sack reduced it to ~2.5-3 ha (Broshi & Finkelstein 1992; Geva 2014).

Ephesus-Turkey.name: Ephesus
Ephesus-Turkey.evidence_basis: LBA Arzawa capital Apasa on Ayasoluk hill succeeding into an Archaic Ionian city of ~55-65 ha clustered around the monumental Artemision rebuilt under Croesus (Bammer; Kerschner).

Carchemish-Turkey.name: Carchemish
Carchemish-Turkey.evidence_basis: MBA/LBA Euphrates crossing and Hittite viceregal capital (~40 ha inner town) expanding to a ~90 ha Neo-Hittite metropolis before Assyrian annexation in 717 BC and the 605 BC battle (Wilkinson et al. 2016; Osborne 2020).

Ebla-Syria.name: Ebla
Ebla-Syria.evidence_basis: Walled 56 ha inner and lower city with Royal Palace G archives in EB IVA (~15,000-18,000) and rebuilt Amorite fortifications in MBA before final Hittite destruction c. 1600 BC (Matthiae 2010; Archi).

Hazor-Israel.name: Hazor
Hazor-Israel.evidence_basis: Largest Canaanite city in the Southern Levant at ~80-84 ha upper and lower town in MBA/LBA (Broshi & Gophna 1986; Ben-Tor), destroyed c. 1230 BC and rebuilt as a ~12 ha Iron II Israelite royal fortress before 732 BC.

Tell Rifaat-Syria.name: Tell Rifaat
Tell Rifaat-Syria.evidence_basis: Capital of Aramean Bit-Agusi covering ~105 ha across tell and walled lower town prior to its three-year siege and capture by Tiglath-Pileser III in 740 BC (Seton-Williams; Osborne 2020).

Arwad-Syria.name: Arwad
Arwad-Syria.evidence_basis: Compact ~40 ha fortified island-city paired with mainland Antaradus, renowned in Assyrian annals for its multi-storey residential density and powerful naval fleet (Markoe 2000).

Samaria-Palestine.name: Samaria
Samaria-Palestine.evidence_basis: Omride capital founded c. 880 BC comprising a ~6 ha royal ashlar acropolis surrounded by ~50 ha of lower slopes and suburbs before the 722 BC Assyrian conquest and conversion into Samerina (Broshi & Finkelstein 1992).

Tayma-Saudi Arabia.name: Tayma
Tayma-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Massive NW Arabian oasis enclosed by a ~14 km outer mudbrick rampart (~800 ha walled oasis with ~20 ha dense urban core), surging to royal prominence during Babylonian King Nabonidus's 552-542 BC residence (Eichmann & Hausleiter 2018).

Kition-Cyprus.name: Kition
Kition-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Major LBA harbour city (~22-25 ha across Kathari and Bamboula sectors) refounded as a Tyrian Phoenician royal colony in the 9th c. BC controlling southeastern Cypriot trade (Karageorghis; Yon).

Gaza-Palestine.name: Gaza
Gaza-Palestine.evidence_basis: Primary LBA Egyptian administrative capital of Canaan evolving into the southernmost Philistine Pentapolis port and Mediterranean terminus of the Arabian incense caravan trade (Katzenstein).

Phocaea-Turkey.name: Phocaea
Phocaea-Turkey.evidence_basis: Archaic Ionian maritime coloniser enclosed by a monumental ~50 ha 6th c. BC stone fortification wall before partial emigration after Harpagus's 546 BC siege (Ozyigit 1994).

Tarsus-Turkey.name: Tarsus
Tarsus-Turkey.evidence_basis: Major Cilician Bronze Age urban mound and lower port (~25-30 ha, Goldman 1956) continuing as Tarsa, chief commercial city of Iron Age Que/Hilakku and seat of the Syennesis dynasty.

Hama-Syria.name: Hama
Hama-Syria.evidence_basis: Large 12 ha Orontes citadel mound plus sprawling Iron II lower town serving as royal capital of Luwian-Aramean Hamath prior to Sargon II's 720 BC sack (Fugmann 1958; Bryce 2012).

Kerkenes Dag-Turkey.name: Kerkenes Dag
Kerkenes Dag-Turkey.evidence_basis: Late 7th c. BC imperial foundation enclosing ~250 ha of sparsely packed urban compounds within a 7 km stone wall, burned and abandoned c. 547 BC after the Lydian-Persian clash (Summers 2017).

Sapinuwa-Turkey.name: Sapinuwa
Sapinuwa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated Hittite royal residence and administrative archive centre spread across ~90 ha of lower terraces at Ortakoy, peaking in the 14th c. BC before severe fire destruction and gradual decline (Suel 2002; Mielke 2011).

Ashkelon-Israel.name: Ashkelon
Ashkelon-Israel.evidence_basis: Massive ~60 ha semicircular earthen-ramparted MBA Canaanite port continuing as a major Philistine Pentapolis city until Nebuchadnezzar II's 604 BC destruction and Persian recovery (Stager et al. 2008).

Byblos-Lebanon.name: Byblos
Byblos-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Fortified ~8-10 ha dense coastal tell plus outer suburbs functioning as Egypt's primary EBA-LBA cedar-export harbour and continuing as a prosperous Iron Age Phoenician kingdom (Dunand; Markoe 2000).

Adana-Turkey.name: Adana
Adana-Turkey.evidence_basis: LBA Kizzuwatna centre of Adaniya rising in Iron II to the ~45 ha royal capital of the House of Mopsos in Hiyawa/Que attested in the Cineköy and Karatepe bilinguals (Bryce 2016; Routledge 2017).

Acemhoyuk-Turkey.name: Acemhoyuk
Acemhoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: MBA primate capital of ~55 ha mound and lower town with monumental Sarikaya and Hatipler palaces (Ozguc 2015; Palmisano 2017), declining sharply following the termination of the Old Assyrian trade network.

Til Barsip-Syria.name: Til Barsip
Til Barsip-Syria.evidence_basis: Fortified ~45-50 ha Euphrates crossing capital of Masuwari/Bit-Adini rebuilt by Shalmaneser III as the major Neo-Assyrian western headquarters Kar-Shalmaneser (Bunnens 1995; Osborne 2020).

Gath-Israel.name: Gath
Gath-Israel.evidence_basis: Largest Philistine city-state spanning ~45-50 ha upper and lower town in Iron I-IIA until Aramean King Hazael's c. 830 BC siege and destruction (Maeir 2012).

Shabwa-Yemen.name: Shabwa
Shabwa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Capital of Hadramawt with 15.5 ha inner royal core, 53.9 ha outer walled precinct, and ~1,500 ha flood-irrigated oasis controlling frankincense transit (Breton 1998).

Palaepaphos-Cyprus.name: Palaepaphos
Palaepaphos-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Polycentric multi-plateau LBA-Iron Age kingdom seat centred on the Sanctuary of Aphrodite, mapped by the PULP urban landscape project (Iacovou 2013).

Guzana-Syria.name: Guzana
Guzana-Syria.evidence_basis: Walled ~50-55 ha Aramean capital of Bit-Bahiani on the Upper Khabur with Kapara palace and Neo-Assyrian governor's archives (Novak 2013; Osborne 2020).

Enkomi-Cyprus.name: Enkomi
Enkomi-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Densely gridded ~15 ha fortified LBA copper-smelting metropolis with ashlar sanctuaries, gradually abandoned c. 1075-1050 BC as harbour silting shifted population to Salamis (Courtois; Iacovou 2013).

Tuwanuwa-Turkey.name: Tuwanuwa
Tuwanuwa-Turkey.evidence_basis: LBA Hittite town in the Lower Land rising in the 8th c. BC to the ~45 ha capital of Warpalawas's Tabalian kingdom of Tuwana guarding the Cilician Gates (d'Alfonso 2012; Massa et al. 2020).

Amathus-Cyprus.name: Amathus
Amathus-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Early Iron Age Eteocypriot royal foundation (~25 ha terraced acropolis, palace, and harbour) growing steadily as a major southern maritime kingdom (Aupert; Hermary).

Maras-Turkey.name: Maras
Maras-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Gurgum (~40 ha mound and lower settlement beneath modern Maras) attested by Hieroglyphic Luwian royal stelae and converted into an Assyrian province in 711 BC (Bryce 2012).

Sirkeli Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Sirkeli Hoyuk
Sirkeli Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Geophysical survey and excavation reveal a ~40-60 ha urban complex (citadel and lower town) on the Ceyhan River with Muwatalli II rock relief and major LBA-Iron II occupation (Novak et al.).

Timna-Yemen.name: Timna
Timna-Yemen.evidence_basis: Walled capital of Qataban in Wadi Bayhan enclosed by a 1,850 m fortification circuit (~22 ha urban core) with monumental pillared halls and irrigated valley estates (de Maigret; Breton).

Alalakh-Turkey.name: Alalakh
Alalakh-Turkey.evidence_basis: Contiguous twin Amuq Valley capitals: 22 ha MBA/LBA Mukish capital at Tell Atchana (Woolley; Yener) followed 900 m north by the ~35-40 ha Iron Age Palistin/Unqi capital of Kunulua at Tell Tayinat (Harrison 2014; Osborne 2020).

Ugarit-Syria.name: Ugarit
Ugarit-Syria.evidence_basis: Excavated 22-26 ha walled cosmopolitan port and palace-archive capital housing ~7,000-10,000 urban residents before its violent destruction and urban abandonment c. 1185 BC (Yon 2006; Schloen 2001).

Arslantepe-Turkey.name: Arslantepe
Arslantepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Late Chalcolithic/EB I palatial hub continuing through Hittite Malitiya into the Neo-Hittite capital of Melid with ~35-40 ha urban extent and smooth post-1200 BC dynastic continuity (Frangipane; Manuelli & Mori 2016; Osborne 2020).

Beirut-Lebanon.name: Beirut
Beirut-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Excavated Bronze and Iron Age glacis-fortified coastal tell (~10-15 ha) attested in Amarna correspondence and expanding under Phoenician-Persian maritime trade (Badre 1998).

Beycesultan-Turkey.name: Beycesultan
Beycesultan-Turkey.evidence_basis: Twin-mound Upper Meander urban centre reaching ~20 ha in EB III (Abay 2011) and ~35 ha with monumental MBA/LBA Burnt Palace complex before Late Bronze collapse (Lloyd & Mellaart 1962; Dedeoglu).

Dedan-Saudi Arabia.name: Dedan
Dedan-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Capital of the Kingdom of Dedan (~40 ha core archaeological zone plus irrigated palm canyon) controlling the northern Hejaz Incense Route (Rohmer & Charloux; Al-Said).

Ekron-Israel.name: Ekron
Ekron-Israel.evidence_basis: Philistine Pentapolis city of ~20 ha in Iron I expanding to ~34 ha in 7th c. BC as the Near East's largest olive-oil industrial hub before Nebuchadnezzar's 604 BC sack (Gitin 1995; Broshi & Finkelstein 1992).

Rabbath-Ammon-Jordan.name: Rabbath-Ammon
Rabbath-Ammon-Jordan.evidence_basis: Capital of the Iron Age Kingdom of Ammon spanning ~20-25 ha across the fortified Jabal al-Qala citadel and lower wadi terraces (Zayadine; LaBianca & Younker 1995).

Hala Sultan Tekke-Cyprus.name: Hala Sultan Tekke
Hala Sultan Tekke-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Magnetometry and excavation reveal a ~25-30 ha LBA trade metropolis on the Larnaca Salt Lake lagoon, violently destroyed and abandoned c. 1150 BC (Fischer & Burge 2017).

Konya-Karahoyuk-Turkey.name: Konya-Karahoyuk
Konya-Karahoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated 21 ha central mound with MBA palaces and an outer fortified lower town bringing settled area to 36-40 ha in 1950-1750 BC, shrinking after its MBA destruction (Alp 1972; Massa et al. 2020).

Liman Tepe-Turkey.name: Liman Tepe
Liman Tepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Major fortified EBA Aegean harbour of ~15 ha (Massa & Sahoglu 2015) evolving into Archaic Ionian Klazomenai (~30 ha settled coastal sector and chora; Koparal et al. 2017).

Qalat al-Bahrain-Bahrain.name: Qalat al-Bahrain
Qalat al-Bahrain-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Walled ~16-18 ha stratified capital and harbour of Dilmun supported by artesian spring oases, mediating Mesopotamian-Magan-Indus maritime commerce (Hojlund & Andersen 1994; Potts 1990).

Akko-Israel.name: Akko
Akko-Israel.evidence_basis: Fortified ~20 ha Canaanite and Phoenician bay-harbour mound continuously occupied from MBA ramparts through Assyrian and Persian naval supply phases (Dothan; Killebrew).

Idalion-Cyprus.name: Idalion
Idalion-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Inland Mesaoria city-kingdom spanning ~30 ha across twin acropolises and lower town controlling Troodos copper transit to the south coast (Hadjicosti; Gaber).

Qarnaw-Yemen.name: Qarnaw
Qarnaw-Yemen.evidence_basis: Orthogonally walled ~10 ha royal capital of the Minaean kingdom (1,150 m perimeter) in the Jawf basin plus surrounding irrigated agricultural villages (Schiettecatte 2011).

Kourion-Cyprus.name: Kourion
Kourion-Cyprus.evidence_basis: LBA urban predecessor at Bamboula shifting to the Iron Age kingdom capital of Kourion attested on the Esarhaddon Prism of 673 BC (Swiny; Iacovou).

Troy-Turkey.name: Troy
Troy-Turkey.evidence_basis: EB II-III citadel and lower town of ~9 ha (Jablonka 2016) expanding in LBA Troy VI-VIIa (Wilusa) to ~27-30 ha with ditched lower city before c. 1180 BC destruction and Archaic Aeolian resettlement (Korfmann; Rose 2014).

Kelainai-Turkey.name: Kelainai
Kelainai-Turkey.evidence_basis: Strategic Phrygian and Lydian royal road hub at the Meander headwaters (~30 ha settled area) becoming a primary Achaemenid satrapal residence after 546 BC (Summerer et al. 2011).

Zincirli-Turkey.name: Zincirli
Zincirli-Turkey.evidence_basis: Circular double-walled Aramean/Neo-Hittite capital of Sam'al covering ~40 ha with excavated residential quarters and bit-hilani palaces (Schloen & Fink 2009; Osborne 2020).

Tripoli-Lebanon.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Iron Age Phoenician maritime emporium established on the Al-Mina promontory by Tyre, Sidon, and Arwad as a tri-partite federal trading port (Markoe 2000).

Samuha-Turkey.name: Samuha
Samuha-Turkey.evidence_basis: Primate MBA city-state (~20 ha, Palmisano 2017) on the Upper Kizilirmak that grew into a major LBA Hittite royal refuge and administrative capital with monumental palace and archive buildings (Muller-Karpe).

Najran-Saudi Arabia.name: Najran
Najran-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Fertile Wadi Najran caravan metropolis (Ragmat in Karib'il Watar's annals) at the northern bifurcation of the South Arabian Incense Route toward Hejaz and the Gulf (Schiettecatte 2011).

Soloi-Cyprus.name: Soloi
Soloi-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Northwestern Cypriot kingdom capital (Assyrian Sillu) controlling the Skouriotissa copper belt and Morphou Bay export harbour (Gjerstad; Iacovou).

Dumat al-Jandal-Saudi Arabia.name: Dumat al-Jandal
Dumat al-Jandal-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Walled northern Arabian oasis stronghold and seat of the Qedarite Arab queens attested in Neo-Assyrian royal annals of Sennacherib and Esarhaddon (Charloux & Loreto 2014).

Sinope-Turkey.name: Sinope
Sinope-Turkey.evidence_basis: Milesian Black Sea colony founded c. 630 BC on a compact ~20 ha twin-harbour peninsula serving as primary Pontic maritime emporium and colonising metropolis (Doonan 2004).

Smyrna-Turkey.name: Smyrna
Smyrna-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~15 ha densely built walled peninsula at Bayrakli housing an estimated 5,000-7,000 Archaic Greek inhabitants prior to Alyattes's c. 600 BC siege mound destruction (Akurgal 1983; Cook).

Tell Afis-Syria.name: Tell Afis
Tell Afis-Syria.evidence_basis: Excavated ~25 ha northern Syrian settlement expanding in Iron II as Hazrek, royal seat of Zakkur of Hamath and Lu'ash (Mazzoni 1995; Venturi 2007).

Emar-Syria.name: Emar
Emar-Syria.evidence_basis: Planned LBA Hittite Euphrates river-port and administrative archive city (~20-25 ha) violently destroyed c. 1185 BC during the Late Bronze collapse (Margueron; Fleming 2000).

Kadesh-Syria.name: Kadesh
Kadesh-Syria.evidence_basis: Strategic Orontes-Homs Gap fortress tell (~10-12 ha plus lower settlement) contested by Egypt and Hatti in the 13th c. BC (Parr; Akkermans & Schwartz 2003).

Tamassos-Cyprus.name: Tamassos
Tamassos-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Copper-rich Troodos foothills kingdom attested as Tamesi in the Esarhaddon Prism, featuring royal ashlar chamber tombs and smelting workshops (Buchholz).

Xanthos-Turkey.name: Xanthos
Xanthos-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of Lycia on a ~25 ha terraced acropolis above the Xanthos River, severely depopulated in Harpagus's c. 545 BC conquest before Persian-era rebuilding (des Courtils).

Marion-Cyprus.name: Marion
Marion-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Excavated western Cypriot coastal kingdom thriving on Limni copper exports and Archaic Aegean trade links (Childs et al. 2012).

Lachish-Israel.name: Lachish
Lachish-Israel.evidence_basis: Fortified ~7-10 ha Shephelah tell and lower residential slopes forming Judah's second city in Level III prior to Sennacherib's 701 BC siege and Nebuchadnezzar's 588 BC destruction (Ussishkin 2004; Broshi & Finkelstein 1992).

Nashshan-Yemen.name: Nashshan
Nashshan-Yemen.evidence_basis: Major fortified ~12 ha Jawf city-state rival of Saba' sacked and reduced in status by Sabaean Mukarrib Karib'il Watar in the early 7th c. BC (Breton; Schiettecatte 2011).

Alaca Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Alaca Hoyuk
Alaca Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: EB III royal cemetery centre and LBA walled Hittite cult city of ~18 ha with monumental Sphinx Gate and palace-temple complex, shrinking to a modest Phrygian village after c. 1180 BC (Mielke 2011; Bryce 2005).

Sarepta-Lebanon.name: Sarepta
Sarepta-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Extensively excavated ~12 ha Phoenician industrial harbour between Tyre and Sidon featuring pottery kilns, olive presses, and murex purple-dye installations (Pritchard 1978).

Raybun-Yemen.name: Raybun
Raybun-Yemen.evidence_basis: Extensive Russian-excavated terraced settlement and sanctuary complex in Wadi Dawan anchoring Hadramawt's interior flood-irrigated agriculture (Sedov 1996).

Dor-Israel.name: Dor
Dor-Israel.evidence_basis: Excavated ~8-12 ha coastal harbour town of the Sikila/Tjeker and Phoenicians becoming the Neo-Assyrian provincial capital of Duru (Sharon & Gilboa 2013; Stern).

Sirwah-Yemen.name: Sirwah
Sirwah-Yemen.evidence_basis: Early Sabaean highland sanctuary-town and fortified ceremonial seat of the Mukarribs featuring the Almaqah temple and Karib'il Watar victory inscriptions (Gerlach).

Dan-Israel.name: Dan
Dan-Israel.evidence_basis: Ramparted ~20 ha MBA city of Laish at the Jordan headwaters, continuing as a major Iron II northern Israelite-Aramean cult and administrative stronghold (Biran 1994).

Lapithos-Cyprus.name: Lapithos
Lapithos-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Major Early/Middle Cypriot necropolis centre evolving into a northern coastal Iron Age city-kingdom facing Cilicia (Gjerstad; Iacovou).

Yathrib-Saudi Arabia.name: Yathrib
Yathrib-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Large volcanic-basin Hejaz date-palm oasis attested as Iatribu in Nabonidus's Harran Stele as the southernmost station of his western Arabian domain.

Alisar Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Alisar Hoyuk
Alisar Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: EB II fortified settlement of 11 ha (von der Osten 1937) expanding to ~20 ha in the MBA karum phase (Palmisano 2017) and flourishing again as a walled Iron Age Alisar IV town.

Ikiztepe-Turkey.name: Ikiztepe
Ikiztepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Multi-mound Kizilirmak delta settlement covering ~25 ha with intensive EBA-MBA metallurgical and maritime activity (candidate for Zalpa), declining after the early Hittite Old Kingdom (Bilgi 2001).

Kinet Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Kinet Hoyuk
Kinet Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~15 ha dual-harbour Cilician emporium on the Gulf of Iskenderun with continuous EBA through Neo-Assyrian and Persian commercial phases (Gates 2015).

Kululu-Turkey.name: Kululu
Kululu-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified Iron Age Tabalian royal hill-city of ~18-20 ha northeast of Kayseri yielding lead strip economic archives and Hieroglyphic Luwian royal inscriptions of Tuwati and Ruwas (Hawkins 2000; Bryce 2012).

Megiddo-Israel.name: Megiddo
Megiddo-Israel.evidence_basis: Strategic Jezreel Valley ~6-10 ha fortified tell plus lower terraces controlling the Via Maris, serving as Canaanite city-state, Israelite chariot centre, and Assyrian provincial capital Magiddu (Finkelstein et al.).

Pella-Jordan.name: Pella
Pella-Jordan.evidence_basis: Spring-fed ~10 ha Jordan Valley fortified tell (Pihilu in Egyptian Execration and Amarna texts) with monumental MBA/LBA migdal temple and Iron Age town (Bourke).

Hili-United Arab Emirates.name: Hili
Hili-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Major ~10 ha core Umm an-Nar fortified tower settlement and date-palm oasis expanding dramatically in Iron II with the earliest archaeologically dated falaj irrigation canals (Cleuziou; Magee 2014).

Trapezus-Turkey.name: Trapezus
Trapezus-Turkey.evidence_basis: Sinopean/Milesian eastern Pontic colony established on a ~15 ha defensible coastal tableland linking Black Sea maritime trade to interior silver and iron mining corridors.

Batroun-Lebanon.name: Batroun
Batroun-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Coastal town attested as Batruna in the Amarna Letters and fortified by Ithobaal I of Tyre in the 9th c. BC behind a rock-cut seawall (Markoe 2000).

Gezer-Israel.name: Gezer
Gezer-Israel.evidence_basis: Heavily fortified ~12-13 ha strategic tell overlooking the Ayalon pass with massive MBA cyclopean walls and Iron II gateworks (Dever; Ortiz & Wolff).

Dibon-Jordan.name: Dibon
Dibon-Jordan.evidence_basis: Fortified ~12 ha Moabite royal capital of King Mesha (Mesha Stele) with monumental acropolis palace and reservoirs before 6th c. BC decline (Routledge 2004; Porter et al.).

Qurayyah-Saudi Arabia.name: Qurayyah
Qurayyah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Excavated ~300 ha walled LBA-EIA oasis with 15 ha fortified acropolis and major ceramic production centre for Qurayyah Painted Ware (Luciani 2018).

Tarut-Saudi Arabia.name: Tarut
Tarut-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Major Early-Middle Bronze Age Gulf island harbour and chlorite-vessel entrepot linked closely to Dilmun and Sumerian maritime trade (Potts 1990; Zarins).

Sarissa-Turkey.name: Sarissa
Sarissa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Planned Hittite provincial foundation of ~18 ha enclosed by casemate walls with acropolis palace and temples, destroyed c. 1200 BC and lightly reoccupied in the Iron Age (Muller-Karpe 2017).

Beth-Shean-Israel.name: Beth-Shean
Beth-Shean-Israel.evidence_basis: Key ~4-6 ha Egyptian LBA garrison headquarters at the Jezreel-Jordan junction continuing as an Iron II Israelite administrative centre until 732 BC (Mazar 2006).

Bozrah-Jordan.name: Bozrah
Bozrah-Jordan.evidence_basis: Fortified ~8-10 ha ridge-top capital of Edom with monumental Assyrian-influenced acropolis temple and palace, severely damaged in Nabonidus's c. 552 BC campaign (Bienkowski 2002; Porter 2004).

Shechem-Palestine.name: Shechem
Shechem-Palestine.evidence_basis: Fortified ~6 ha central hill-country pass city with MBA migdal temple and LBA Labayu stronghold, reviving in Iron II before 724 BC Assyrian destruction (Wright; Campbell).

Bat-Oman.name: Bat
Bat-Oman.evidence_basis: UNESCO-listed Umm an-Nar monumental stone-tower oasis settlement and extensive necropolis in interior Magan (Oman) flourishing on Bronze Age copper production and Iron II falaj revival (Thornton et al. 2016).

Oluz Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Oluz Hoyuk
Oluz Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~15 ha Pontic inland mound in the Amasya plain expanding through Phrygian/Iron II urban phases into a major Persian-era administrative town (Donmez 2010).

Nerik-Turkey.name: Nerik
Nerik-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~12-15 ha northern Hittite Storm-God cult capital at Oymaagac Hoyuk, disrupted by Kaska raids in the 14th c. BC and restored under Hattusili III and Tudhaliya IV (Czichon; Archi 2023).

Palmyra-Syria.name: Palmyra
Palmyra-Syria.evidence_basis: Desert spring oasis settlement (Tell under Temple of Bel) attested in Old Assyrian, Mari, and Middle Assyrian Tiglath-Pileser I texts as a caravan staging post (al-Maqdissi).

Salut-Oman.name: Salut
Salut-Oman.evidence_basis: Excavated Iron Age fortified hilltop citadel and extensive falaj-irrigated oasis complex in central Oman (Avanzini & Degli Esposti 2018).

Hebron-Palestine.name: Hebron
Hebron-Palestine.evidence_basis: Fortified ~4-5 ha southern Judean highland mound with MBA cyclopean fortifications and Iron II royal lmlk administrative jar sealings (Chadwick; Broshi & Finkelstein 1992).

Amisos-Turkey.name: Amisos
Amisos-Turkey.evidence_basis: Phocaean/Milesian Black Sea port founded c. 564 BC on the Toraman Tepe headland controlling the central Pontic caravan route from the Anatolian plateau.

Mersin-Yumuktepe-Turkey.name: Mersin-Yumuktepe
Mersin-Yumuktepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Stratified ~8 ha Cilician coastal mound featuring massive LBA Hittite casemate fortifications and Iron Age coastal village/town phases (Garstang 1953; Caneva).

Jericho-Palestine.name: Jericho
Jericho-Palestine.evidence_basis: Spring-fed ~4 ha fortified oasis mound peaking in EBA III and MBA II before c. 1550 BC destruction and modest Iron II Judahite reoccupation (Kenyon; Nigro).

Failaka-Kuwait.name: Failaka
Failaka-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Excavated Bronze Age Dilmun Gulf island settlement and temple complex at Tells F3 and F6 mediating Ur-Dilmun maritime exchange (Hojlund 1987; Potts 1990).

Muweilah-United Arab Emirates.name: Muweilah
Muweilah-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Excavated fortified Iron II oasis trading town near Sharjah featuring a columned civic hall and domestic camel economy before its c. 600 BC fire destruction (Magee 2014).

Tapikka-Turkey.name: Tapikka
Tapikka-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~10 ha Hittite frontier garrison palace and archive town guarding the northeastern Kaska borderlands (Ozguc 1978), followed by modest Phrygian/Iron Age settlement.

Hesbon-Jordan.name: Hesbon
Hesbon-Jordan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~5 ha Madaba Plains highland citadel and reservoir town contested between Ammon and Moab during Iron I-II (LaBianca & Ray).

Tell el-Umeiri-Jordan.name: Tell el-Umeiri
Tell el-Umeiri-Jordan.evidence_basis: Heavily fortified ~6 ha Ammonite ramparted mound south of Amman yielding royal Baalis seal impressions and well-preserved Iron I-II domestic quarters (Herr et al.).

Khirbat en-Nahas-Jordan.name: Khirbat en-Nahas
Khirbat en-Nahas-Jordan.evidence_basis: Major ~10 ha Iron I-IIA industrial copper-smelting complex and square fortress in Wadi Faynan supporting several thousand miners and smelters before 8th c. BC contraction (Levy et al. 2014).

Tell Deir Alla-Jordan.name: Tell Deir Alla
Tell Deir Alla-Jordan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~4-5 ha central Jordan Valley trade, copper-working, and cult sanctuary mound renowned for the Iron II Aramaic Balaam plaster inscription (Franken; van der Kooij).

Tell Abraq-United Arab Emirates.name: Tell Abraq
Tell Abraq-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Continuously occupied ~4 ha Gulf coastal mound anchored by a 40 m diameter Umm an-Nar stone fortress tower spanning Bronze through Iron II trade networks (Potts 2000).

Hegra-Saudi Arabia.name: Hegra
Hegra-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Pre-Nabataean Iron Age/Dedanite caravan oasis settlement documented in deep soundings below the later Hegra residential zone (Nehme et al.).

Qaryat al-Faw-Saudi Arabia.name: Qaryat al-Faw
Qaryat al-Faw-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Early caravan station at the Tuwayq Escarpment pass linking Najran to Gerrha/Dilmun prior to its later expansion as the Kinda capital (Al-Ansary 1982).

Tell Habuba Kabira and Habuba Kabira Sou.name: Tell Habuba Kabira and Habuba Kabira South

Karatepe-Turkey.name: Karatepe
Karatepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Late 8th c. BC fortified border citadel and outer town (~5-6 ha) built by Azatiwatas of Adana with monumental Phoenician-Luwian bilingual orthostats before c. 680 BC destruction (Cambel; Bryce 2012).

Dervish of Soliman and Selim II 16C-Syri.name: Dervish of Soliman and Selim II 16C

Kadhima Areas ABC, E, F and G-Kuwait.name: Kadhima Areas ABC, E, F and G

Tawilan-Jordan.name: Tawilan
Tawilan-Jordan.evidence_basis: Largest excavated unfortified Edomite agricultural town (~5 ha) near Petra yielding Neo-Babylonian Harran cuneiform economic tablet and domestic compounds (Bennett & Bienkowski 1995).

Shisr-Oman.name: Shisr
Shisr-Oman.evidence_basis: Limestone-sinkhole desert spring oasis in Dhofar showing Bronze and Iron Age frankincense caravan staging occupation prior to later Classical fortification (Zarins 2001).

Cave with Dedication (Zeus, Hera, and Ar.name: Cave with Dedication (Zeus, Hera, and Ares

Kilise Tepe-Turkey.name: Kilise Tepe
Kilise Tepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~4 ha fortified Goksu Valley settlement controlling the inland corridor from the Konya Plain to the Mediterranean port of Ura (Postgate & Thomas 2007; Massa et al. 2020).

En Hazeva-Israel.name: En Hazeva
En Hazeva-Israel.evidence_basis: Strategic Arava Valley spring oasis with ~1 ha monumental Judahite-Edomite fortress and surrounding caravan settlement guarding the Arabian incense route (Cohen & Yisrael).

Tell el-Kheleifeh-Jordan.name: Tell el-Kheleifeh
Tell el-Kheleifeh-Jordan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~2 ha casemate-walled Edomite-Judahite Red Sea entrepot at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba mediating incense and maritime trade (Pratico 1993).

Beersheba-Israel.name: Beersheba
Beersheba-Israel.evidence_basis: Completely excavated ~1.5-2 ha planned oval Judahite Negev administrative town with tripartite storehouses and water system destroyed in 701 BC (Herzog 2016).

Tuleilat Qasr Musa Hamid IA Settlement-I.name: Tuleilat Qasr Musa Hamid IA Settlement
